g.text: LyonRank3Convo2 begins.
If I may, I wish to tell you a story of a stray alley cat who used to come by the back of the church.
Go on.
Why?
[Ignore.]
Thank you.
I fear it would take more effort to explain than it would be worth.
Chat ends.
Though I suspect that this tale is not unique to this scruffy old tom, and my interactions with him seemingly noteworthy, it bears telling all the same.
Never mind.
Every day he would come by to beg scraps and whatever meagre affections he could have from me or the other brothers and sisters who doted upon him.
Chat ends.
He was a ragged thing, with a limp in his leg and missing part of an ear.
When he did not come by for a few days, Marie was quite beside herself with worry. But what is one to do for an old alley tom who has met their end, save to issue up a prayer to Lua?
Update boolean LyonStray
[Let him continue.]
Is that allowed in your religion? Praying for animals, I mean.
You would pray for the soul of a departed alley cat?
Regardless, imagine my surprise when I was fetching bread from the market and I saw the old tom sitting next to the owner of the stand.
+10 Chemistry
Of course. Some of the purest, brightest souls I have encountered were encased in the flesh of a beast. It is not for me to judge how the Luminaries have set them upon their paths.
He greeted me with a raspy meow, as he always did, and hopped down to rub against my leg.
A good question. In some sects, no. It would be seen as heresy. But in ours, yes. We recognize that animals have souls.
Saint Elizabeth the Wise was known for her charity toward animals, though many traditions to do not recognize the Saints as apostles of the Luminaries.
And I would note, Drifter, that he did so without a limp.
I find myself wondering if any influence of our order survived this long... but it was hardly the point of the conversation.
"Ah, one of Old Devereaux's fools, I see." The man laughed as he bagged up my bread.
Update boolean LyonLecture1
It turns out the old cat was playing us, and several others, in the neighborhood. He was not starving, of failing health, or neglected in any way.
Indeed, if the man's words were to be believed, he was quite a murderous fiend in regards to the local population of birds.
Did you stop feeding Old Devereaux when he came around?
Are you trying to warn me about Roathe?
Are you the alley cat in this story?
+10 Chemistry
There are a great many things to warn you about the devil "Cardinal Dimanche" put upon our doorstep. Perhaps this is one of them. Perhaps it is not.
The Luminaries know I have certainly been worn at the edges as of late. But is this meant to stand as a warning about myself? Perhaps. Perhaps it is not.
No, we did not. In fact, Marie greeted him with all the more affection for it, teasing him for being "her little imp."
It is simply a story to say that sometimes, when a creature seems to be in need -
But we no longer fretted over him. We knew that Old Devereaux could quite adequately care for himself. He did not need us.
+15 Chemistry
What happened to Old Devereaux, do you know?
What do you think drove Old Devereaux to visit you, if it wasn't need?
- check to see how sharp its claws may be.
His next disappearance, two years later, turned permanent.
The cynical answer I would supply you with would be "greed." For if one could have one feast, why not two? Why not ten?
Chat ends.
Did you pray for him?
I hope he left this world comfortable and loved.
What would be the non-cynical answer?
Does that remain the same if he was only seeking affection?
I lit a candle for him the night I learned of his death and prayed to Lua to guide his soul to... wherever she would guide a little imp like him.
May I ask why?
+10 Chemistry
An avaricious desire for affection is still gluttony, though it is not a hunger fed by meat and wine. And to seek it in such false pretenses?
And thanked Old Devereaux for all the joy he brought Marie in exchange for all those coveted bits of chicken gristle and head scratches.
He was an animal. He was just searching for fulfillment - food, shelter, love - he wasn't inspired by the same motivations as people. He wasn't "lying," he was hunting with a different set of tools.

I have seen a lot of violence, Lyon. A lot of it I have caused. I have come to hope that everyone, no matter who they are or what they've done, can have a peaceful death surrounded by those who love them.
I found myself oddly... respecting the cat, for the place it had found itself in the world.
He was a cat, Lyon. He hardly knew what he was doing.
We are still speaking about a cat, yes?
Thank you. I will not hinder you in your day any longer.
He wasn't denying others anything by making you all his "fools." If anything... you all seem to have been enriched by his visits.
Fascinating. I would expect you to despise your enemies. But that is my own folly - to assume I know how anyone in this day and age would comport themselves.
Here was a creature who had learned to use its condition - its appearance, its age, its scars - as a weapon against "the fools" around him who did not see through his ruse.
He knew well enough to feign a limp.
Infer from this conversation whatever you wish, Drifter.
-F. Lyon Allard
Add -1 to Thermostat
Add 1 to Thermostat
An imp in matted fur, he truly was. Yet I found myself petting him all the same when he came 'round to visit.
Chat ends.
Yes. I suppose we were. And we were not experiencing a shortage of bits of chicken gristle and scratches.
Let alone someone with your particularly fascinating upbringing.
And equally heartbroken when, two years later, his next disappearance was permanent.
Perhaps that is why I lit a candle for him and prayed to Lua to take his soul and guide it to... wherever she would take a little imp like him.
+5 Chemistry
+5 Chemistry
Thank you. I will not hinder you in your day any longer. This has been a most interesting conversation. Until we speak again.
And why I thanked Old Devereaux in my prayers that night for all the joy he had brought Marie.
-F. Lyon Allard
Perhaps his little villainy was of some good in a roundabout manner.
Chat ends.
